problem.summary: 单图像超分辨率（SISR）在大的放大因子（如4倍）下，难以恢复精细的纹理细节。基于优化的方法（如最小化均方误差MSE）虽然能获得较高的峰值信噪比（PSNR），但生成的图像缺乏高频细节，感知质量不佳，无法匹配高分辨率图像应有的保真度。

motivation.summary: 现有方法过度依赖像素级损失函数（如MSE），导致生成的图像过于平滑，缺乏照片真实感。需要一种能够生成感知上令人信服、具有照片真实感纹理的超分辨率方法。

core_idea.summary: 提出SRGAN，一个用于图像超分辨率的生成对抗网络（GAN）。通过结合对抗损失和基于感知相似性的内容损失（而非像素空间相似性），将生成的超分辨率图像推向自然图像流形，从而恢复照片真实的纹理。

method.summary: 1. 生成器：采用深度残差网络（ResNet），包含多个残差块和子像素卷积层进行上采样。2. 判别器：一个卷积网络，用于区分真实的高分辨率图像和生成的超分辨率图像。3. 感知损失函数：由内容损失（基于预训练VGG网络的特征图）和对抗损失（来自判别器）加权组合而成。

experiments.summary: 在Set5、Set14和BSD100基准数据集上进行4倍超分辨率实验。评估指标包括PSNR、SSIM和平均意见得分（MOS）。与多种现有方法（如双三次插值、SRCNN、SelfExSR、DRCN、ESPCN等）进行比较。进行了消融研究，探索不同内容损失（MSE、VGG2.2、VGG5.4）的影响。

claims.claim: SRGAN是第一个能够为4倍放大因子推断出照片真实感自然图像的框架。
SRGAN在感知质量（MOS得分）上显著优于现有方法，其MOS得分更接近原始高分辨率图像。
基于VGG深层特征的内容损失（VGG5.4）结合对抗损失，能产生感知上最令人信服的结果。
标准定量指标（PSNR/SSIM）无法准确评估与人类视觉系统相关的图像质量。
SRResNet（基于MSE优化）在PSNR/SSIM上达到了新的最优水平。

limitations.limitation: 模型并非为实时超分辨率设计，计算效率不是重点。
在少数情况下，SRGAN可能产生轻微的重建伪影。
理想的损失函数可能因应用而异。
PSNR/SSIM指标与感知质量不匹配，但论文未提出新的定量感知指标。

nodes.title: 生成器网络 (G)
nodes.label: Generator Network
nodes.summary: 一个深度残差网络，用于从低分辨率输入图像生成高分辨率超分辨率图像。
nodes.description: 生成器网络G以低分辨率图像ILR为输入，输出超分辨率图像ISR。其核心是B个残差块，每个块包含两个3x3卷积层、批归一化和PReLU激活。通过两个训练的子像素卷积层提高分辨率。网络参数为θG = {W1:L, b1:L}。

nodes.title: 判别器网络 (D)
nodes.label: Discriminator Network
nodes.summary: 一个卷积网络，用于区分真实的高分辨率图像和生成器生成的超分辨率图像。
nodes.description: 判别器网络D被训练以解决最大化问题（公式2），区分真实HR图像IHR和生成的SR图像G(ILR)。它包含八个卷积层，使用Leaky ReLU激活（α=0.2），避免使用最大池化。

nodes.title: 感知损失函数 (l_SR)
nodes.label: Perceptual Loss Function
nodes.summary: 由内容损失和对抗损失加权组合而成的损失函数，用于训练生成器。
nodes.description: 感知损失l_SR定义为内容损失l_SR^X和对抗损失的加权和（公式3）。内容损失可以是像素级MSE损失（公式4）或基于VGG网络特征图的感知损失（公式5）。对抗损失l_SR^Gen基于判别器对生成图像的概率（公式6）。

nodes.title: 内容损失 (l_SR^X)
nodes.label: Content Loss
nodes.summary: 衡量生成图像与真实高分辨率图像在内容上的相似性，可以是像素级或特征级。
nodes.description: 内容损失有两种形式：1) 像素级MSE损失（公式4），计算HR图像和SR图像像素值的均方误差。2) VGG损失（公式5），基于预训练VGG网络中特定层（i,j）的特征图φi,j计算均方误差，衡量感知相似性。

nodes.title: 对抗损失 (l_SR^Gen)
nodes.label: Adversarial Loss
nodes.summary: 鼓励生成器产生能够欺骗判别器的图像，使其分布接近真实图像分布。
nodes.description: 对抗损失l_SR^Gen定义为生成图像G(ILR)的判别器概率D(G(ILR))的负对数之和（公式6）。最小化此损失等价于最大化判别器将生成图像误判为真实图像的概率。

nodes.title: 训练过程
nodes.label: Training Process
nodes.summary: 交替优化生成器和判别器，使用随机梯度下降（Adam优化器）最小化感知损失。
nodes.description: 训练图像对(IHR, ILR)来自ImageNet。ILR通过对IHR进行高斯滤波和4倍下采样获得。使用Adam优化器（β1=0.9）。生成器通过最小化感知损失l_SR进行优化（公式1）。判别器通过解决公式2中的最大化问题进行优化。VGG损失的特征图被缩放以匹配MSE损失的尺度。

edges.label: 生成器输出用于计算损失
edges.description: 生成器G的输出G(ILR)被输入到感知损失函数l_SR中，用于计算内容损失和对抗损失。

edges.label: 判别器输出用于计算对抗损失
edges.description: 判别器D对生成图像G(ILR)的输出概率D(G(ILR))被用于计算对抗损失l_SR^Gen。

edges.label: 内容损失是感知损失的一部分
edges.description: 内容损失l_SR^X（MSE或VGG损失）是感知损失l_SR的组成部分。

edges.label: 对抗损失是感知损失的一部分
edges.description: 对抗损失l_SR^Gen是感知损失l_SR的组成部分。

edges.label: 感知损失用于优化生成器
edges.description: 在训练过程中，通过最小化感知损失l_SR来优化生成器G的参数θG（公式1）。

edges.label: 判别器在训练中被优化
edges.description: 在训练过程中，判别器D的参数θD通过解决公式2中的最大化问题进行优化。

deltas.before: 使用像素级MSE损失作为优化目标。
deltas.after: 使用由内容损失（VGG特征损失）和对抗损失组成的感知损失函数。
deltas.why_it_matters: MSE损失导致生成的图像过于平滑，缺乏高频纹理细节。感知损失（特别是VGG深层特征损失）能更好地捕捉感知相似性，而对抗损失能将图像推向自然图像流形，从而生成照片真实的纹理。

deltas.before: 优化目标是最大化PSNR/SSIM等定量指标。
deltas.after: 优化目标是生成感知质量高、照片真实的图像，通过MOS测试评估。
deltas.why_it_matters: PSNR/SSIM与人类感知质量不匹配。SRGAN通过优化感知损失和进行MOS测试，直接针对感知质量进行优化和评估，生成更令人满意的图像。

deltas.before: 网络架构可能较浅或未充分利用残差学习。
deltas.after: 采用非常深的残差网络（ResNet）作为生成器，并引入子像素卷积层进行上采样。
deltas.why_it_matters: 更深的网络能建模更复杂的映射，残差学习有助于训练，子像素卷积能高效地提高分辨率。这些架构改进提升了生成器的容量和性能。

formulas.description: 生成器参数θG的优化目标：最小化训练集上感知损失l_SR的平均值。

variables.name: \hat{\theta}_G
variables.description: 优化后的生成器网络参数

variables.name: \theta_G
variables.description: 生成器网络G的参数（权重和偏置）

variables.name: l_{SR}
variables.description: 感知损失函数，是内容损失和对抗损失的加权和

variables.name: G_{\theta_G}(I^LR_n)
variables.description: 生成器对第n个低分辨率输入图像的输出（超分辨率图像）

variables.name: I^HR_n
variables.description: 第n个真实的高分辨率图像

formulas.intuition: 这是生成器训练的核心优化公式。目标是找到一组参数，使得生成器对所有低分辨率输入生成的图像，与对应的高分辨率真实图像之间的感知损失最小。

formulas.description: 标准的GAN min-max目标函数，用于训练判别器D和生成器G。

variables.name: D_{\theta_D}(\cdot)
variables.description: 判别器网络，输出输入图像是真实图像的概率

variables.name: p_{train}(I^{HR})
variables.description: 真实高分辨率图像的训练数据分布

variables.name: p_G(I^{LR})
variables.description: 低分辨率输入图像的分布（由高分辨率图像下采样得到）

formulas.intuition: 判别器试图最大化正确分类真实和生成图像的概率，而生成器试图最小化判别器正确分类其生成图像的概率。这个对抗过程促使生成器产生更逼真的图像。

formulas.description: 像素级均方误差（MSE）损失函数。

variables.name: W, H
variables.description: 低分辨率图像的宽度和高度

variables.name: I^{HR}_{x,y}
variables.description: 高分辨率图像在位置(x,y)的像素值

variables.name: G_{\theta_G}(I^{LR})_{x,y}
variables.description: 生成的超分辨率图像在位置(x,y)的像素值

formulas.intuition: 最常用的超分辨率损失，直接比较像素值。虽然能获得高PSNR，但倾向于产生平滑的图像，缺乏纹理细节。

formulas.description: 基于预训练VGG网络特征图的感知损失函数。

variables.name: \phi_{i,j}
variables.description: 在预训练VGG网络中，第i个最大池化层之前、第j个卷积层之后的ReLU激活层的特征图

variables.name: W_{i,j}, H_{i,j}
variables.description: VGG网络中相应特征图的宽度和高度

formulas.intuition: 在VGG网络的特征空间中计算损失，而不是像素空间。深层特征（如VGG5.4）更关注图像内容和语义，能更好地衡量感知相似性，有助于生成更清晰的纹理。

formulas.description: 生成器的对抗损失，旨在最大化判别器将生成图像误判为真实图像的概率。

variables.name: D_{\theta_D}(G_{\theta_G}(I^{LR}_n))
variables.description: 判别器对第n个生成图像输出的“真实”概率

formulas.intuition: 最小化此损失等价于最大化判别器犯错的概率，从而鼓励生成器产生更逼真的图像。使用-log D(G(ILR))而不是log(1-D(G(ILR)))是为了在训练初期提供更强的梯度。

glossary.SRGAN: 超分辨率生成对抗网络，本文提出的方法。
glossary.SISR: 单图像超分辨率，从单张低分辨率图像恢复高分辨率图像的任务。
glossary.PSNR: 峰值信噪比，一种基于像素差异的图像质量评估指标，单位为分贝(dB)。
glossary.SSIM: 结构相似性指数，一种衡量两幅图像结构相似性的指标。
glossary.MOS: 平均意见得分，一种主观的图像质量评估方法，由人类评分者给出1-5分。
glossary.MSE: 均方误差，像素级损失函数，计算两幅图像对应像素差值的平方的平均值。
glossary.VGG网络: 一种深度卷积神经网络架构，常用于特征提取。本文使用预训练的VGG19网络。
glossary.感知损失: 基于高层特征（如VGG特征）而非像素值计算的损失函数，旨在衡量感知相似性。
glossary.对抗损失: 来自判别器的损失，鼓励生成器产生能欺骗判别器的图像。
glossary.残差块: 包含跳跃连接的网络块，用于训练非常深的网络。
glossary.子像素卷积: 一种上采样操作，通过卷积和像素重排来提高特征图分辨率。
glossary.批归一化: 一种训练技术，通过归一化层输入来稳定和加速训练。
glossary.PReLU: 带参数的线性整流单元，一种激活函数。
glossary.Leaky ReLU: 带泄漏的线性整流单元，一种激活函数，允许小的负梯度。
glossary.Adam优化器: 一种自适应学习率的随机梯度下降优化算法。
glossary.ImageNet: 一个大型图像数据库，常用于预训练和评估计算机视觉模型。

steps.description: 1. 数据准备：从ImageNet采样35万张图像，通过高斯滤波和4倍下采样生成LR-HR图像对。
2. 网络构建：实现生成器（16个残差块，子像素卷积上采样）和判别器（8个卷积层）网络。
3. 损失函数：实现MSE损失、VGG特征损失（基于VGG19的特定层）和对抗损失。
4. 训练：使用Adam优化器（β1=0.9）交替优化生成器和判别器。将LR输入缩放到[0,1]，HR目标缩放到[-1,1]。VGG特征图缩放约1/12.75。
5. 评估：在Set5, Set14, BSD100上计算PSNR/SSIM（在Y通道上，中心裁剪，去除4像素边界）。进行MOS测试。

metadata.title: Photo-Realistic Single Image Super-Resolution Using a Generative Adversarial Network
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Generative Models / GAN / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: Despite the breakthroughs in accuracy and speed of single image super-resolution using faster and deeper convolutional neural networks, one central problem remains largely unsolved: how do we recover the finer texture details when we super-resolve at large upscaling factors? The behavior of optimization-based super-resolution methods is principally driven by the choice of the objective function. Recent work has largely focused on minimizing the mean squared reconstruction error. The resulting estimates have high peak signal-to-noise ratios, but they are often lacking high-frequency details and are perceptually unsatisfying in the sense that they fail to match the fidelity expected at the higher resolution. In this paper, we present SRGAN, a generative adversarial network (GAN) for image super-resolution (SR). To our knowledge, it is the first framework capable of inferring photo-realistic natural images for 4x upscaling factors. To achieve this, we propose a perceptual loss function which consists of an adversarial loss and a content loss. The adversarial loss pushes our solution to the natural image manifold using a discriminator network that is trained to differentiate between the super-resolved images and original photo-realistic images. In addition, we use a content loss motivated by perceptual similarity instead of similarity in pixel space. Our deep residual network is able to recover photo-realistic textures from heavily downsampled images on public benchmarks. An extensive mean-opinion-score (MOS) test shows hugely significant gains in perceptual quality using SRGAN. The MOS scores obtained with SRGAN are closer to those of the original high-resolution images than to those obtained with any state-of-the-art method.

Abstract
Despite the breakthroughs in accuracy and speed of single image super-resolution using faster and deeper con- volutional neural networks, one central problem remains
largely unsolved: how do we recover the ﬁner texture details
when we super-resolve at large upscaling factors? The
behavior of optimization-based super-resolution methods is principally driven by the choice of the objective function.
Recent work has largely focused on minimizing the mean

squared reconstruction error. The resulting estimates have high peak signal-to-noise ratios, but they are often lacking high-frequency details and are perceptually unsatisfying in the sense that they fail to match the ﬁdelity expected at the higher resolution. In this paper, we present SRGAN, a generative adversarial network (GAN) for image super- resolution (SR). To our knowledge, it is the ﬁrst framework capable of inferring photo-realistic natural images for 4× upscaling factors. To achieve this, we propose a perceptual loss function which consists of an adversarial loss and a content loss. The adversarial loss pushes our solution to
the natural image manifold using a discriminator network

that is trained to differentiate between the super-resolved images and original photo-realistic images. In addition, we use a content loss motivated by perceptual similarity instead of similarity in pixel space. Our deep residual network is able to recover photo-realistic textures from heavily downsampled images on public benchmarks. An extensive mean-opinion-score (MOS) test shows hugely signiﬁcant gains in perceptual quality using SRGAN. The MOS scores obtained with SRGAN are closer to those of the original high-resolution images than to those obtained with any state-of-the-art method. 1. Introduction The highly challenging task of estimating a high- resolution (HR) image from its low-resolution (LR) counterpart is referred to as super-resolution (SR). 1.1.1 Image super-resolution

Recent overview articles on image SR include Nasrollahi and Moeslund [43] or Yang et al. [61]. Here we will focus on single image super-resolution (SISR) and will not further discuss approaches that recover HR images from multiple images [4, 15]. Prediction-based methods were among the ﬁrst methods to tackle SISR. While these ﬁltering approaches,e.g. linear, bicubic or Lanczos [14] ﬁltering, can be very fast, they oversimplify the SISR problem and usually yield solutions with overly smooth textures. Methods that put particularly focus on edge-preservation have been proposed [1, 39]. More powerful approaches aim to establish a complex mapping between low- and high-resolution image informa- tion and usually rely on training data. Many methods that are based on example-pairs rely on LR training patches for which the corresponding HR counterparts are known. Early work was presented by Freeman et al. [18, 17]. Related ap- proaches to the SR problem originate in compressed sensing [62, 12,...

algorithms have shown excellent performance. In Wang et al. [59] the authors encode a sparse representation prior into their feed-forward network architecture based on the learned iterative shrinkage and thresholding algorithm (LISTA) [23]. Dong et al. [9, 10] used bicubic interpolation to upscale an input image and trained a three layer deep fully convolutional network end-to-end to achieve state- of-the-art SR performance. Subsequently, it was shown that enabling the network to learn the upscaling ﬁlters directly can further increase performance both in terms of accuracy and speed [11, 48, 57]. With their deeply-recursive convolutional network (DRCN), Kim et al. [34] presented a highly performant architecture that allows for long-range pixel dependencies while keeping the number of model parameters small. Of particular relevance for our paper are the works by Johnson et al. [33] and Bruna et al. [5], who rely on a loss function closer to perceptual similarity to recover visually mor...
1.1.2 Design of convolutional neural networks

The state of the art for many computer vision problems is meanwhile set by speciﬁcally designed CNN architectures following the success of the work by Krizhevsky et al. [37]. It was shown that deeper network architectures can be difﬁcult to train but have the potential to substantially increase the network’s accuracy as they allow modeling mappings of very high complexity [49, 51]. To efﬁ- ciently train these deeper network architectures, batch- normalization [32] is often used to counteract the internal co-variate shift. Deeper network architectures have also been shown to increase performance for SISR, e.g. Kim et al. [34] formulate a recursive CNN and present state-of-the- art results. Another powerful design choice that eases the training of deep CNNs is the recently introduced concept of residual blocks [29] and skip-connections [30, 34]. Skip- connections relieve the network architecture of modeling the identity mapping that is trivial in nature, however, po- tentially non-trivi...

Pixel-wise loss functions such as MSE struggle to handle the uncertainty inherent in recovering lost high-frequency
details such as texture: minimizing MSE encourages ﬁnd-
ing pixel-wise averages of plausible solutions which are typically overly-smooth and thus have poor perceptual qual- ity [42, 33, 13, 5]. Reconstructions of varying perceptual

inpainting. Bruna et al. [5] minimize the squared error in

the feature spaces of VGG19 [49] and scattering networks. Dosovitskiy and Brox [13] use loss functions based on Euclidean distances computed in the feature space of neural networks in combination with adversarial training. It is shown that the proposed loss allows visually superior image generation and can be used to solve the ill-posed inverse problem of decoding nonlinear feature representa- tions. Similar to this work, Johnson et al. [33] and Bruna et al. [5] propose the use of features extracted from a pre- trained VGG network instead of low-level pixel-wise error measures. Speciﬁcally the authors formulate a loss function based on the euclidean distance between feature maps extracted from the VGG19 [49] network. Perceptually more convincing results were obtained for both super-resolution and artistic style-transfer [19, 20]. Recently, Li and Wand [38] also investigated the effect of comparing and blending patches in pixel or VGG feature space.

1.2. Contribution GANs provide a powerful framework for generating plausible-looking natural images with high perceptual qual- ity. The GAN procedure encourages the reconstructions to move towards regions of the search space with high probability of containing photo-realistic images and thus closer to the natural image manifold as shown in Figure 3. In this paper we describe the ﬁrst very deep ResNet [29, 30] architecture using the concept of GANs to form a perceptual loss function for photo-realistic SISR. Our main contributions are: • We set a new state of the art for image SR with high upscaling factors (4×) as measured by PSNR and structural similarity (SSIM) with our 16 blocks deep ResNet (SRResNet) optimized for MSE. • We propose SRGAN which is a GAN-based network optimized for a new perceptual loss. Here we replace the MSE-based content loss with a loss calculated on feature maps of the VGG network [49], which are more invariant to changes in pixel space [38]. • We conﬁrm with...
large margin, for the estimation of photo-realistic SR

images with high upscaling factors (4×). We describe the network architecture and the perceptual loss in Section 2. A quantitative evaluation on public bench- mark datasets as well as visual illustrations are provided in Section 3. Of particular importance when aiming for photo-realistic

solutions to the SR problem is the choice of the content loss as illustrated in Figure 6. In this work, we found lSR VGG/ 5.4 to yield the perceptually most convincing results, which we attribute to the potential of deeper network layers to represent features of higher abstraction [68, 65, 40] away from pixel space. We speculate that feature maps of these deeper layers focus purely on the content while leaving the adversarial loss focusing on texture details which are the main difference between the super-resolved images without the adversarial loss and photo-realistic images. We also note that the ideal loss function depends on the application. For example, approaches that hallucinate ﬁner detail might be less suited for medical applications or surveillance. The perceptually convincing reconstruction of text or structured scenes [31] is challenging and part of future work. A.3. Mean opinion score (MOS) testing In all conducted MOS tests we have asked 26 human raters to assign a score from 1 (Bad) to 5 (Excellent) to reconstructions of the 4× downsampled versions of images from Set5, Set14 and BSD100. On BSD100 nine versions of each image were rated by each rater. On Set5 and Set14 the raters also rated three additional versions of the proposed methods to investigate
different content losses. In total 26*100*9 + 26*14*12 + 26*5*12 = 29328 ratings were obtained, where each rater rated 1128

images. Images were presented in a completely randomized fashion without any indication of the employed super-resolution approach. The raters were calibrated on images not included in the testing set such that the nearest neighbor interpolated reconstruction should receive score 1 (Bad) and the original high-resolution image score 5 (Excellent). The distribution of MOS ratings on each individual data set is summarized in Figure 9. The average ordinal rank over all corresponding ratings of an image and rater are shown in Figure 10. Note that a score of 1 corresponds to the best rank and ranks are averaged for samples that would have the same ordinal ranking. While results on Set5 are somewhat inconclusive due to very small
sample size and images with comparably little detail, ratings on Set14 and especially on the large BSD100 data set conﬁrm

that SRGAN is signiﬁcantly better than any compared state-of-the-art method. In fact, MOS ratings obtained with SRGAN are closer to those of the original high-resolution images than to those obtained with any reference method. Set5 Set14 BSD100
